title: The Poisson distribution
overview: Model random events over a fixed time/space interval with the Poisson distribution, and know when it approximates the binomial. This guide turns the current syllabus outcomes into a connected revision sequence: learn the ideas, practise the method, then use the recall cards and checklist to diagnose what still needs work.
syllabusPoints: Calculate probabilities for X~Po(λ) and use E(X)=Var(X)=λ.
Scale λ with time, area or volume.
Recognise conditions for a Poisson process.
Use Poisson approximations to binomial and normal approximations to Poisson.

definitions.definition: A count model for random events occurring independently at a constant average rate.
The expected number of events in the stated interval; it is also the variance.
Expected events per unit time, length, area or volume.
A ±0.5 boundary adjustment for a continuous normal approximation.
An event with small probability per trial, supporting a Poisson approximation to binomial.

sections.title: Poisson probabilities
content: If X~Po(λ), then P(X=r)=e⁻ˡᵃᵐᵇᵈᵃ λʳ/r!, r=0,1,2,… . Mean and variance are λ. Use cumulative or complementary probabilities for ranges.
bullets: State the interval to which λ applies.

sections.title: Scaling the parameter
content: A rate of c per unit gives λ=ct over t units, provided the rate is constant. Independent Poisson counts on disjoint intervals add, so parameters add too.
bullets: Scale λ, not an observed count.
Check that units match before multiplying.

sections.title: Poisson approximation to binomial
content: For X~B(n,p), use Po(np) when n is large and p small; Cambridge gives approximately n>50 and np<5. The approximation removes the fixed upper bound, so use only when the tail beyond n is negligible.
bullets: No continuity correction is needed for Poisson-to-binomial because both are discrete.

sections.title: Normal approximation to Poisson
content: When λ is large—approximately λ>15—use N(λ,λ) and apply a continuity correction. Standardise with standard deviation √λ.
bullets: Correct the integer boundary before finding z.
Sketch the tail to avoid complement errors.

examTips: Write the newly scaled λ before computing any probability.
Distinguish an exact Poisson model from a Poisson approximation in your notation.
Show the mathematical setup and exact working before the final rounded answer; unsupported calculator output may not earn method marks.
commonMistakes: Using λ as a standard deviation.
Forgetting to scale λ when the interval changes.
Applying a normal approximation without continuity correction.

quickRecall.question: What are the mean and variance of Po(λ)?
How does λ change when an interval triples?
quickRecall.answer: It triples if the average rate stays constant.

quickRecall.question: When is Poisson a useful binomial approximation?
quickRecall.answer: For large n and small p, approximately n>50 and np<5 in this syllabus.

quickRecall.question: What normal model approximates Po(λ)?
quickRecall.answer: N(λ,λ), with a continuity correction, when λ is sufficiently large.
